cards.back: It produces content—such as text or images—from learned patterns and the input available now. Making a draft is different from checking that everything in it is true.
cards.example: It can write the invitation. You check the date and the details.

cards.recallPrompt: Is the model the whole app?
cards.back: A model is the trained component that processes input and produces output. The product around it can add instructions, memory, files, search and other models.
cards.example: Different product features can change the result, even when the task stays the same.

cards.recallPrompt: Does the whole answer have to be wrong?
cards.back: No. A hallucination is false or unsupported content in an AI answer. One invented detail can sit inside otherwise useful work.
cards.example: The invitation gets both days right but says a table is booked when nobody made a reservation.

cards.back: A difference in how often groups use a technology. It measures participation, not ability. A group's lower use does not tell you what an individual woman can do.
cards.example: An adoption survey cannot establish whose AI-assisted work is better.
